description: The I-95 Exit 2 interchange at SR 452 (Market Street) includes traffic improvements to convert the I-95 northbound ramp intersection from a two-way stop to a fully signalized intersection with pedestrian accommodations. A dedicated left-turn lane will be provided for southbound SR 452 traffic turning left onto the I-95 NB entrance ramp. Dual left-turn lanes will be provided for I-95 northbound exit ramp onto northbound SR 452. At the I-95 southbound ramp intersection with Chestnut Street and S R452, re-striping of the SR 452 lanes will shift the offset left turn lanes so they are aligned and will accommodate two SR 452 northbound through-lanes to be carried through the entire interchange. Signal and pedestrian upgrades on the intersection are included.Â The project will involve minor roadway widening, traffic signal upgrades, right-of-way acquisition, drainage improvements, and utility relocations. This segment of 452 is on the Walk Roll Delco Active Transportation Plan. This is a breakout of MPMS #79329 - Bridgewater Road Extension.

title: US 322 over CSX (Bridge)
description: Replacement of the bridge carrying SR 322 over CSX and Bethel Road as well as improvements to the Bethel Road Interchange. Includes improvements of 1-mile section of SR 322 extending west from the SR 322/I-95 interchange. Project improvements include pavement reconstruction and reprofiling to improve the vertical clearance over Bethel Road and CSX railroad. The SR 322/Bethel Road interchange will be reconfigured to include standard acceleration and deceleration lane lengths and increased curve radii. Bethel Road will be reconstructed at the SR 322 interchange and drainage improvements will be installed between Excelsior Drive to Keystone Road. The project also includes new traffic signals at the intersections of Highland Avenue and Bethel Road and SR 452 and I-95 northbound ramps, and traffic signal upgrades at the intersection of Township Line Road and Renshaw Road. A final alternative for bridge replacement was determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Haverford Road Corridor Safety Improvements
description: Construction of a partial road diet which would create a lane configuration of two lanes eastbound, one lane westbound, and a two-way center left turn lane from Landover Road (SR 1001) to Karakung Road/Winchester Road. This project would also include updated traffic signal equipment, installation of exclusive left turn lanes at signalized intersections, and modifications to left turn signal phasing. This corridor is on the Walk Roll Delco Active Transportation Plan.

title: Victory Avenue over SEPTA Norristown High Speed Line
description: This project will replace the bridge on Victory Avenue over SEPTA's Norristown High Speed Line in Delaware County. This road segment is included in the Walk Roll Delco Active Transportation Plan

title: US 202 and US 1 Intersection Area Improvements
description: This project is in Concord and Chadds Ford Townships and involves intersection improvements to ease congestion. Improvements include pavement widening, pavement reconstruction and signal upgrades to accommodate an additional northbound US 1 travel lane through the intersection and a double left turn lane for northbound US 202. Other roadway improvements will include landscaped medians throughout the project area; eastbound and westbound left turn lanes and a signalized US 202 pedestrian crossing at the US 202/State Farm Drive/Brandywine Drive intersections; and signalized pedestrian crossings at the US 1/Applied Bank Boulevard/State Farm Drive intersection. Project CMP commitments include sidewalks, crosswalks, and enhanced bus stop areas in consultation with SEPTA. See DVRPC's 2013-2014 memorandum on supplemental strategies for details related to this project.

title: Lloyd Street Bridge Over Amtrak/SEPTA Wilmington Newark Rail Line (CB)
description: The Lloyd Street Bridge, which was constructed in 1899, served the industrial waterfront, was in poor condition and removed. This project will replace the bridge with a single span composite weathering steel plate girder bridge accommodating two twelve foot lanes with six foot shoulders and seven foot sidewalks on both sides.

title: Concord Road / Bethel Road / Engle Street Intersection Improvement (Sec DBE)
description: The project includes intersection improvements at the Concord Road/Bethel Road intersection and the Concord Road/Engle Street intersection. The two intersections are separated by 400 feet along Concord Road. A Roundabout is proposed at Concord/ Bethel Roads and stop-controlled intersection Improvements are proposed at Concord Road/ Engle Street. The project will involve minor roadway upgrades, right-of-way acquisition, and utility relocations. Both Engle Street and Concord Rd are on the Walk Roll Delco Active Transportation Plan. This is a breakout of MPMS #79329 - Bridgewater Road Extension.

title: Media Bypass ITS (Competitive CMAQ)
description: The purpose of this project is to help reduce congestion, improve traffic flow and reduce emissions along the Route 1 corridor by adding ITS elements to the corridor. This project proposes the following work: installation of four (4) changeable message signs (CMS) and fourteen (14) CCTV cameras, along SR 0001 between the intersections at Schoolhouse Lane and Weymouth Road, and installation of underground fiber. This project also includes safety improvements to the SR 0001 and SR 0252 Interchange by installing a new left turn lane from SR 0252 northbound to SR 0001 southbound and associated signal upgrades to facilitate exclusive left turn phasing. Funding for this project will be drawn down from the Competitive CMAQ Line Item (MPMS# 48201) at the appropriate time. The Route 252 road segment is included in the Walk Roll Delco Active Transportation Plan.

title: Eastern Delaware County Bikeway Implementation Plan (TOP)
description: This project will implement concepts of The Eastern Delaware County Bikeway Prioritization Study, that was previously funded through a DVRPC TCDI grant. The project will also create a connected bicycle network through the four municipalities of Upper Darby, Lansdowne, East Lansdowne, and Yeadon. The network will connect neighborhoods to regional trails, such as the Darby Creek Trail, the Cobbs Creek Trail, and the Bike Baltimore Avenue Route, as well as schools, parks, transit stations, other areas of interest, and the established bicycle network in the City of Philadelphia. This conceptual network was developed through a comprehensive stakeholder and public involvement process and will serve to encourage and promote bicycle usage throughout the region. A high-quality bicycle network will allow cyclists to use these routes for both recreational and commuting purposes, thus reducing their dependence on cars and single occupancy vehicle (SOV) trips. Furthermore, it will allow for connection opportunities to neighboring municipalities to the west including Aldan, Haverford, Clifton Heights, Darby, and Springfield and may encourage further investment in bicycle options in other areas of Delaware County. This project includes investments in many heavily urbanized, dense, and economically distressed communities and will provide more affordable travel options for those with limited access to automobiles who may be dependent on non-motorized or public transportation. It will also provide another option for commuters who may decide to bike to work or to transit stations. Due to the connections to schools and parks, it will also provide safer opportunities for students to get to schools and recreational areas nearby. This may, in turn, take much of the burden off parents who may not be available to transport them nor the option to work from home. The projects that will be completed as part of the TOP grant are as follows: 1) Bywood Road, Fairfield Ave and Connectors 2) Baltimore Ave to Philadelphia 3) Bywood, Stonehurst, and Beverly Hills Connectors 4) West Baltimore Ave and Gladstone Connectors 5) Chestnut St 6) Garrett Rd--Multi-Use Connector

title: 3rd Street Dam Over Broomall Lake
description: This project will replace the partially breached Third Street Dam over Broomall's Run with a 150 ft pedestrian and bicycle bridge. The project also includes roadway drainage, stream restoration, stormwater management, and naturalized aesthetic improvements.

title: Mattson Road over the West Branch of the Chester Creek
description: This project is for the bridge rehabilitation or replacement of the County-owned Mattson Road bridge spanning over the West Branch of the Chester Creek in Chester Heights Borough, Delaware County. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement is determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance. This project is a $5 fee matching funds (sSTP) project.

title: US 13 Safety: Calcon Hook Rd to Main Street
town: Collingdale Borough, Darby Borough, Sharon Hill Borough
description: The following countermeasures are proposed as part of this project: • Install hardened centerlines on major street approaches at all signalized intersections (Calcon Hook Road, Laurel Road, MacDade Boulevard-Chester Pike, Springfield Road, and Main Street.) • Redefine intersection space with curb extensions at Calcon Hood Road and redefine one-way street and alley access between Laurel Road and Greenwood Street. • Install two curb extensions at Chestnut Street to improve visibility and intersection alignment. • Install two-way left turn lane by repurposing excess roadway space between Calcon Hook Road and Laurel Road. • Signage/pavement marking – Restripe parking lanes with 6 inch wide pavement markings between Greenwood Street and MacDade Boulevard) to visually narrow roadway and redefine travel lanes. • Install high visibility crosswalks at signalized intersections along the corridor. • Install a hybrid road diet between Springfield Road and Main Street by removing one northbound lane and converting to a painted median. Use painted median to provide space for turning movements. • Provide a section of median island between Springfield Road and Main Street, at Chestnut Street, to assist with access management by limiting movements. (Create opportunity for evaluating future pedestrian midblock crosswalk.) • Provide additional access management between Springfield Road and Main Street by limiting allowable movements and consolidating driveways. • Install dynamic signal warning flashers in two locations on the corridor: in advance of the south approach of the SR 0013/MacDade Boulevard-Chester Pike intersection and the south approach of the MacDade Boulevard/Main Street intersection. These countermeasures will target angle and rear-end crashes and aim to slow vehicle speeds along the corridor and at intersections.

title: Belmont Avenue and St. Asaphs Road Intersection
description: This project will implement safety improvements at the intersection of Belmont Avenue and St. Asaphs Road in Lower Merion Township. In addition to the intersection safety improvements, a partial road diet is proposed on St. Asaphs Road which would create a lane configuration of two lanes eastbound, one lane westbound, and a two-way center left turn lane from Conshohocken State Road to Belmont Avenue. A full road diet is proposed on St. Asaphs Road creating a lane configuration of one lane eastbound, one lane westbound, and a two-way center left turn lane from Belmont Avenue to Monument Road/Presidential Boulevard.

title: PA 23/Valley Forge Road and North Gulph Road Relocation (2NG)
description: This project will relocate a section of existing Valley Forge Road (PA Route 23) and North Gulph Road (SR 3039) to allow for a new "gateway" area for the Valley Forge National Historical Park (VFNHP). Valley Forge Road's alignment will be relocated and widened between County Line Road and North Gulph Road, with a new four-leg intersection approximately 300 feet to the east of the existing park entrance. North Gulph Road will be relocated and widened between Richards Road and the new intersection. The existing PA Route 23 on-ramp to eastbound US Route 422 will be eliminated, with traffic needing to use the on-ramp at First Avenue. Traffic signalization at the relocated intersection of PA 23 and North Gulph Road will be updated. Additional improvements include drainage improvements, new stormwater management facilities, trail improvements, utility relocations and new landscaping. Approximately 1,000 linear feet of trail will be constructed within VFNHP from the park entrance area south to Richards Road. The 10- foot-wide trail will be constructed along the existing North Gulph Road cartway from a connection with the Joseph Plumb Martin Trail in the vicinity of the VFNHP Visitors Center. This project is part (1) of the "River Crossing Complex," which is a complex area of roadways, interchanges, intersections, and bridges in and around the Valley Forge National Historic Park. Environmental clearance for various components was undertaken through MPMS #46954, and individual projects have been broken out as follows: 1) PA 23/US 422 Interchange and North Gulph Road Improvements (MPMS #66952). 2) US 422/PA 363 Interchange, including providing movements to/from the west (MPMS #64796). Project is completed. 3) US 422 Exwy Bridge over the Schuylkill River, replacement of the existing bridge (MPMS #70197), and a new parallel four (4) lane bridge and relocation of PA 23 eastbound off-ramp as an expressway fly-over. Project is completed. 4) US 422 Widening for 1.8 miles from PA-363 interchange to the US-202 interchange. This project has not yet been broken out. 5) Old Betzwood Bridge Bike/Pedestrian Trail will be re-built as a bike/pedestrian bridge only, and will not re-instate vehicular traffic (MPMS# 16703). Project is completed. 6) An early action interim project to provide timely and effective relief to westbound afternoon congestion until the long range projects can fully advance was programmed and constructed as MPMS #74648. Project is completed. The River Crossing complex projects have received the following federal earmarks: 2008 Appropriation (PA ID# 711) -$735,000 - repurposed SAFETEA-LU (FED ID# 0020/PA ID# 672) -Originally $20,000,000. Balance available $6,080,779. TEA-21 (FED ID# 0140/PA ID# 088) -No funds remain.

title: Ridge Pike: Harmon Road to Crescent Avenue
description: This project involves full-depth reconstruction of the Ridge Pike roadway and drainage system, upgrading and interconnecting traffic signals, new sidewalks, improved transit stops, and adding turn lanes at major intersections such as Butler Pike, Joshua Road, and Crescent Avenue. The project extent is from Harmon Road in Plymouth Township to Crescent Avenue in Whitemarsh Township, and is known as Section C of Montgomery County's Ridge Pike Improvement Project program. East of Crescent Avenue, Montgomery County has completed the reconstruction and widening of Ridge Pike as a separate County-funded project (known as Section D). CMP (Congestion Management Process) project commitments include signal upgrades, new sidewalk connections, turning movement enhancements, and emergency vehicle signal pre-emption. See DVRPC's 2010 memorandum on supplemental strategies for details related to this project.

title: Woodmont Road Bridge Replacement (CB #10)
description: The project will involve the replacement of the bridge that carries Woodmont Road over Arrowmink Creek, located in West Conshohocken Borough. The bridge was constructed in 1932. It is anticipated that the proposed bridge will be replaced on the existing horizontal alignment with minimal approach work to tie back into existing conditions. To maintain access to nearby properties during the construction process, half width construction will be investigated. A final alternative for bridge replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Airy Street over Markley Street/SEPTA
description: The Airy Street Bridge over Markley Street (SR 3020), SEPTA train tracks and Stony Creek was built in 1977. The existing bridge is a 5-span steel multi- beam bridge, approximately 529' long. The bridge includes a pedestrian bridge that ramps down to Markley Street on the northeast side. The bridge carries one-way westbound traffic (two lanes) and has an annual average daily traffic (AADT) of approximately 7,164 vehicles per day. The existing bridge has a posted speed limit of 25 miles per hour. Airy Street is owned by the Norristown Municipality, while the bridge is owned by PennDOT (SR 3009). The proposed bridge will replace the existing bridge on the same alignment with a three span bridge that will accommodate two lanes of traffic, a sidewalk on the north side and a shared use path on the south side. The proposed bridge is a multi-span composite steel plate girder bridge with a 26'-0" curb- to-curb dimension and a 43'-11 1/4" out-to-out dimension founded on one stub and one full-height concrete abutment. The bridge barrier on the north side is anticipated to be a 3'-6" tall vertical wall concrete barrier on raised sidewalk. A 4'-3" tall aluminum protective barrier will be installed on top of the concrete barrier in span 3 over the SEPTA railroad and Markley Street. The concrete barrier may receive architectural treatment on the inside and outside faces to fit the site context. The bridge barrier between the travel lanes and the shared used path on the south side is anticipated to be a 3'-6" tall F-shape concrete barrier, which may receive architectural treatment on the outside face (towards the shared use path) to fit the site context. A 6'-9" tall aluminum protective barrier will be installed on the outside of the shared use path in span 3 over the SEPTA railroad and Markley Street. The approach roadway work on the west side of the bridge will include minor reprofiling and pavement reconstruction for approximately 170' to the intersection with Astor Street. The approach roadway work on the east side of the bridge will include minor reprofiling and pavement reconstruction for approximately 400' to the intersection with Barbadoes Street. Approximately 325' of the approach roadway will be on retained fill with retaining walls on both sides. New sidewalk will be installed on the north side of Airy Street and frontage road and a shared use path will be installed on the south side. Because the project consists of a complete bridge replacement, Airy Street will be closed to traffic throughout the duration of construction. A full detour of Airy Street is anticipated during construction. The project may require right-of-way acquisition to accommodate the roadway reconstruction at the approaches and the new bridge abutment and pier at the western span. Temporary construction easements will be required for E&S controls and construction access.

title: Belmont Ave RR Replacement
description: This project involves the replacement of a Norfolk Southern railroad bridge over Belmont Avenue in Lower Merion Township. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: I-76 Overhead Bridges
description: This project involves the replacement of the structures carrying Weadley Road, Gypsy Lane, and Spring Garden Street over Interstate 76 (Schuylkill Expressway) in Upper Merion Township and West Conshohocken Borough. Spans will be lengthened to accommodate widening for Flex Lanes on I-76. Flex lanes will provide increased capacity on I-76 during peak periods and to allow for dynamic lane management during emergency operations, weather events and maintenance activities. Vertical clearance over I-76 will be improved to current standards. The project also includes minor approach roadway reconstruction along Weadley Road, Gypsy Lane, and Spring Garden Street to accommodate the new structures. Locations include: Weadley Road between South Gulph Road and Old Weadley Road in Upper Merion Township. Gypsy Lane between South Gulph Road and Hughes Road in Upper Merion Township. Spring Garden Street between Chestnut Street and Spruce Lane in West Conshohocken Borough.

title: Sumneytown Pike Intersections Safety Improvements
description: The project is along Sumneytown Pike (PA Route 63) in Upper Salford Township, and involves full-depth widening to accommodate the addition of left- turn lanes at the intersection with Ridge Road/Old Skippack Road and Barndt Road, installation of new traffic signals, and geometry updates to improve the skew of the Ridge Road/Old Skippack Road approaches to PA Route 63.

title: Tookany Creek Parkway Bridge Over Tookany Creek
description: This project involves rehabilitating or replacing the weight-limit posted Tookany Creek Parkway bridge over a tributary of the Tookany Creek in Cheltenham Township, just east of New 2nd Street. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: US 202, Markley Street Southbound (Section 500)
description: This project serves as the parent for the pre-construction phases of the Markley Street rehabilitation project for Section 500 of US 202 (SR 3020 and Norristown Borough Street); from approximately 700 feet south of Main Street (local street) to Johnson Highway (SR 3017) for a total length of approximately 8,500 linear feet; and on Johnson Highway (SR 3017) from Markley Street to Powell Street (local street) for a total length of approximately 2,200 feet. Between Main Street (local street) and Marshall Street (local street), Markley Street is a four-lane divided street with no parking permitted. Between Marshall Street and Johnson Highway (SR 3017), it is a two-lane street, with parking typically permitted on both sides. This parent project will incorporate all pre-construction phases (UTL and ROW) for MPMS #80021 (Section 510), #80022 (Section 520), #106068 (Section 530) and Section 540, which will be used for the respective construction contracts. Sections 510, 520 and 530 have already finished construction. In the DVRPC region, US 202 covers 61 miles, traversing 27 municipalities. It serves as a major commuter route and is a vital link for business and industry. For planning purposes, US 202 has been divided into seven major sections (100 through 700), and some of those sections have been broken down further to simplify construction management. Project CMP (Congestion Management Process) commitments include strategies such as improvements for transit users, bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers on the existing road network (operations). See DVRPC's 2007 and 2011 annual memoranda on supplemental strategies for details related to this project.

title: Fruitville Road Bridge Over Perkiomen Creek (CB #232)
description: This project involves rehabilitating or replacing the existing Fruitville Road bridge structure, that is comprised of a stone masonry viaduct with two (2) 3-span stone masonry arch spans and a 110'-long steel, pin connected, Pratt thru truss span that carries Fruitville Road over the Perkiomen Creek and its related floodplain area. The bridge is currently closed to traffic. The final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement will be determined upon federal National Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Cross County Trail East - Section A
description: This project is proposed to develop a multi-use trail from the existing Cross County Trail near Dryden Road in Upper Dublin Township to Maryland Road near Easton Road in Upper Moreland Township. The Cross County Trail is part of the Circuit Trails network and this segment will serve as an important local and regional transportation resource. The Circuit is a planned 800 mile interconnected network of multi-use trails spanning Greater Philadelphia with Philadelphia and Camden as its hub, and is included in DVRPC's Long-Range Plan. Existing and future Circuit Trails are required to meet minimum design standards (10-feet wide, paved, and separated from traffic with limited exceptions) to reflect their intended use as the arteries of a dedicated, regional, non-motorized transportation system.

title: South Collegeville Road (PA 29) at Perkiomen Boulevard
description: This project will complete two through lanes in each direction along PA State Route 29 from US 422 into Collegeville Borough. The additional through lanes will aim to provide significant congestion relief and safety improvements for this busy stretch of road. Additionally, sidewalk will be installed along this section of PA 29, as well as ADA ramps and push buttons at the signalized intersection of PA 29 and Perkiomen Boulevard. A direct connection to Montgomery County's Perkiomen Trail will also be provided.

title: PA 611 Bridge over PA Turnpike Willow Grove Interchange Ramps
description: The project will replace a bridge on Easton Road (PA State Route 611) over Pennsylvania Turnpike's Willow Grove interchange ramps (PennDOT bridge key 27506) that currently has a fair rating. Replacement of the bridge is necessary to modernize the Willow Grove interchange with PA Route 611, allowing for additional traffic flow on southbound PA Route 611 to access the Turnpike by replacing & lengthening the bridge over the interchange ramps to accommodate a two lane southbound access ramp, among other improvements. These modernizations were discussed in Montgomery County's Turnpike Corridor Reinvestment Study.

title: High Street Safety:Hanover St to Washington St
description: The implementation of safety countermeasures will reduce conflicts and improve the overall safety of the corridor. The treatments proposed as part of this project include: Install pedestrian refuge islands Add leading pedestrian intervals Install retroreflective backplates Upgrade signal cabinets Install curb bump outs Install ADA ramps Install high visibility crosswalks

title: Cross County Trail Extension
description: This project is proposed to extend the Cross County Trail from its current terminus at the Germantown Pike/Chemical Road intersection in Plymouth Township east to Joshua Road in Whitemarsh Township. It will include a new pedestrian-only bridge over Germantown Pike and a 1.9-mile trail segment. To the maximum extent feasible, the trail will be designed and constructed to meet multi-use Circuit Trail standards, including an off-road alignment and a paved width of 10-12'. This trail extension will be multi-use and not strictly for recreational purposes. Federal earmark funds were awarded to this project under the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023 in the amount of $2,500,000. The Cross County Trail is part of The Circuit Trails network and this segment will serve as an important local and regional transportation resource. The Circuit is a planned 800-mile interconnected network of multi-use trails spanning Greater Philadelphia with Philadelphia and Camden as its hub, and is included in DVRPC's Long-Range Plan. Existing and future Circuit Trails are required to meet minimum design standards (10-feet wide, paved, and separated from traffic with limited exceptions) to reflect their intended use as the arteries of a dedicated, regional, non-motorized transportation system.

title: North Narberth Avenue Bridge Over Amtrak/SEPTA (CB)
description: This project involves replacing a Narberth Borough-owned, through-girder type bridge over Amtrak-owned railroad tracks. The bridge currently has one sidewalk.This project is subject to standard PennDOT design procedures as defined in the Bicycle/Pedestrian Facilities checklist; the bicycle and pedestrian checklists will be incorporated into the project.

title: Ridge Pike - School Lane to Belvoir Road (CB #0 and TPK Bridge DB-116)/Interchange Area
description: Bridges This project is the combined replacement of Montgomery County Bridge #0 and Pennsylvania Turnpike Bridge DB-116. County Bridge #0 carries Ridge Pike over Norfolk Southern railroad tracks and is 200 feet east of Turnpike Bridge DB-116, which carries Ridge Pike over Interstate 276 (Pennsylvania Turnpike at mile post 331.8). Both structures flank the eastbound on and off ramps of the future Pennsylvania Turnpike Lafayette Street Interchange, and are in poor condition. Montgomery County has designated this project as "Section A" of the Ridge Pike Improvement Project; this is a companion project to MPMS #48175 and #92839, which together make up "Section B".

title: Cheltenham Ave Safety: Broad St to N 15th St
description: The Cheltenham Avenue corridor project is a four-lane undivided highway that stretches 0.17 miles through Cheltenham Township in Montgomery County. The countermeasures proposed as part of this project include: Install a raised concrete median island along Cheltenham Avenue from Broad St to 50 west of N Broad Street Install a pedestrian refuge island at N 15th St Install retroreflective backplates Upgrade signal cabinets Install high visibility crosswalks

title: Main Street Safety Improvements: Egypt to Forrest/Airy
description: The project will implement a 4-lane partial road dietconfiguration along Main Street (SR 3009) between Egypt Road (SR 4002) and Forrest Avenue/West Airy Street in West Norriton Township. The existing four-lane undivided roadway will maintain two (2) through lanes in the westbound direction, one (1) lane eastbound, and a shared left-turn lane throughout the project limits, with dedicated turn lanes at the signalized intersections. The existing traffic signals at Egypt Road/Orchard Lane, Schuylkill Avenue, Whitehall Road, and Forrest Avenue/West Airy Street will be upgraded. The ADA and pedestrian facilities along the corridor will be evaluated and updated as necessary to meet current ADA standards. Signal and temporary easements will be required.

title: Montgomery County 3R Betterments Line Item
description: Reserve Line Item for improvements to County owned roads.

title: PA 309 Connector HT4
description: This project is proposed to make improvements along PA State Route 63 (Sumneytown Pike) near Mainland Road and Old Forty Foot Road in Towamencin Township to improve traffic flow through the eastern edge of the previously completed PA 309 Connector Section HAT project (MPMS #16438). The scope includes reconfiguring access from Mainland Road onto PA Route 63, and increasing left turn lane capacity along PA Route 63 onto the Pennsylvania Turnpike Northeast Extension (I-476) southbound slip ramp at the Forty Foot Road intersection.

title: Perkiomenville Road over Sciota Creek Bridge Replacement
description: This project involves the replacement of a state-owned bridge located on Perkiomenville Road over Scioto Creek in Upper Frederick Township, Montgomery County. The existing bridge, built in 1932, is a one-span concrete closed spandrel arch with a span length of 30 feet. The bridge is two lanes wide with no shoulders or sidewalk. The existing approach roadway is 21 feet wide with two lanes and no shoulders or sidewalk. The bridge is currently posted at 36 tons/40 tons for combination vehicles.

title: Valley Green Road Bridge Over Wissahickon Creek
description: This project involves the replacement of the existing West Valley Green Road bridge over Wissahickon Creek. Constructed in 1884, it is a 174' long, three-span, wrought iron, pin-connected Pratt pony truss. The bridge carries two lanes of traffic on a narrow 18'-8" curb-to-curb width. The bridge was determined eligible for the National Register of Historic Places for its technological significance. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance..

title: Henderson/Gulph Road Widen near I-76 Ramps
description: This project includes construction for widening to four lanes along South Henderson Road from South Gulph Road to Queens Drive, as well as widening to four lanes along South Gulph Road from the approach of Crooked Lane to the eastbound I-76 ramp/PA Route 320 intersection in Upper Merion Township. This is Phase 2 of the project. See MPMS #68064 for Phase 1. CMP (Congestion Management Process) project commitments include ITS treatments, new and expanded park-and-ride facilities, and improvements for bicyclists, pedestrians, and transit users. See DVRPC's 2010 memorandum on supplemental strategies for details related to this project.

title: US 202, Township Line Road to Morris Road (61N)
description: This project will widen and improve 2.8 miles of US Route 202 (DeKalb Pike) from Township Line Road to just south of Morris Road in Whitpain Township, as well as the widening and reconstruction of Route 73 from Whitney Drive to Center Square Fire Company. PennDOT is reconstructing and widening US Route 202 from two lanes to five lanes with a center turn lane, installing five-foot bicycle lanes in both directions along the entire project area, and building new sidewalks and ADA ramps at various locations along the corridor. The project will reconstruct five precast concrete box culverts, two retaining walls, one sound wall, install new traffic signals, traffic cameras, and dynamic message signs, as well as stormwater management and drainage improvements. The project also involves considerable aerial and underground utility relocations and installations on US Route 202 and PA Route 73. This section is designed under Section 610. MPMS #50364 (US 202 Section 610) contained the final design funding for this project. See additional MPMS #'s 63491, 63486, and 63490 for other construction sections of Section 600. In the DVRPC region, US 202 covers 61 miles, traversing 27 municipalities in Delaware, Chester, Montgomery, and Bucks counties. For planning purposes, US 202 has been divided into seven major sections (100 through 700), and some of those sections have been broken down further to simplify construction management. Project CMP (Congestion Management Process) commitments include strategies such as improvements for transit users, bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers on the existing road network (operations). See DVRPC's 2007 annual memoranda on supplemental strategies for details related to this project. TOLL CREDIT

title: Cross County Trail: WissahickonTrail - SEPTA's Fort Washington Station
description: This project is proposed to develop a multi-use trail from the existing Wissahickon Trail in Fort Washington State Park to the existing Cross County Trail near SEPTA's Fort Washington Station in Whitemarsh Township. The Cross County Trail is part of the Circuit Trails network and this segment will serve as an important local and regional transportation resource. The Circuit is a planned 800-mile interconnected network of multi-use trails spanning Greater Philadelphia with Philadelphia and Camden as its hub, and is included in DVRPC's Long-Range Plan. Existing and future Circuit Trails are required to meet minimum design standards (10-feet wide, paved, and separated from traffic with limited exceptions) to reflect their intended use as the arteries of a dedicated, regional, non-motorized transportation system.

title: Belmont Rd/Rock Hill Rd Widening: I-76 Ramps to Rock Hill Road
description: This project proposes to widen Belmont Avenue from two to four lanes along with intersection improvements and streetscape improvements between Jefferson Street and Rock Hill Road. This project will also include improvements at the nearby intersection of Conshohocken State Road and Rock Hill Road. CMP (Congestion Management Process) project commitments include signal upgrades, safety treatments, improvements for bicyclists and pedestrians, and turning movement enhancements. See DVRPC's 2009 memorandum on supplemental strategies for details related to this project. $21.214M out of an estimated $69M (2023 CON estimate of $46.739M) is programmed for construction in FY36. The construction balance that is not shown in FY36 is in the Long-Range Plan. There is a breakout for the separate replacement of the Norfolk Southern railroad bridge over Belmont Avenue in MPMS #82074.

title: Dekalb Street Two-Way Reconstruction
description: The project will fund full-depth reconstruction of the final remaining segment of US 202 in Montgomery County, along with restriping and traffic signal installation to permit two-way traffic along DeKalb Street from Lafayette Street to Johnson Highway in the Municipality of Norristown.

title: Washington Street over Norfolk Southern Railroad
description: This project will replace in its entirety a poor condition bridge carrying Washington Street over Norfolk Southern railroad tracks, connecting downtown Pottstown to the South Pottstown neighborhood and Industrial Highway. A final alternative for bridge replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: PA 309 Connector: Souderton Pike to PA 309 (HT3)
description: The PA 309 Connector Project is intended to create an improved connection between PA Route 63 (near the Lansdale Pennsylvania Turnpike interchange of Interstate 476) and PA Route 309 (near the southern terminus of the Sellersville Bypass) in Bucks County. Phase 1, which created a bypass around Mainland village in Lower Salford and Towamencin Townships, and reconstructed and widened Wambold Road from PA Route 63 (Sumneytown Pike) to Allentown Road, was carried under MPMS #16438. Phase 2 is listed under MPMS #77211 and extended Wambold Road on a new alignment to Cowpath Road, along with upgrading a portion of Township Line Road. Phase 3 will reconstruct and widen Township Line Road between Hatfield-Souderton Pike and the Sellersville Bypass, along with creating a physical connection to PA Route 309. Township Line Road will be widened and the intersection of Bethlehem Pike and Township Line Road will be completely reconstructed to include additional turn lanes. The proposed connector will continue after the intersection of Bethlehem Pike into Bucks County to follow existing Fairhill Road, and the existing bridge over PA Route 309 will be reconstructed. The interchange will consist of two ramps; the existing Fairhill Road segment will become a cul-de-sac and will not connect to the new connector road. Along Bethlehem Pike, improvements will be made to the Bergey Road, Church Road and Unionville Road intersections to the south and Spur Road and County Line Road intersections to the north. The northern intersection of Bethlehem Pike and County Line Road will be the location of a proposed roundabout to improve safety and traffic flow.

title: PA 29 & PA 113
description: This project will improve the intersection of Gravel Pike (PA State Route 29) and Bridge Road (PA State Route 113) in Perkiomen Township by making turning improvements at all four approaches and upgrading signals and ADA ramps. Alternatives are currently being considered.

title: Lancaster Avenue and Remington Road Intersection Improvements
description: The scope of this project entails safety countermeasures which include: 1) Expanding from a four lane to five lane section along Lancaster Ave to add left turn lanes. 2) Install pedestrian countdown timers 3) Add signal (additional primary head) on the mast arms along Remington Road. 4) Provide ADA ramps 5) Upgrade existing mast arms

title: Philmont Avenue/Tomlinson Road/Pine Road Improvements - 6 Point Intersection
description: This project proposes to operationally improve the six-legged intersection of Philmont/Tomlinson/Pine Roads in Lower Moreland Township by converting it into a 5-way approach, dual-lane roundabout.Â Construction will be completed in Â two stages by removing both northern and southern legs of Tomlinson Road, together with the northern Pine Road approach, Â from the intersection and relocating them. Additional shoulder and turning lane improvements along Philmont Avenue and Pine Road are also proposed.Â Â Modernization of the signal equipment intersection of Byberry Avenue/Philmont Avenue on the border of Philadelphia and Montgomery County, together with upgrades (dynamic envelope pavement markings and quad gate installation) to the SEPTA grade crossing on Tomlinson Road have been added toÂ the existing scope ofÂ this project.

title: US 202, Johnson Highway to Township Line Road (61S)
description: This project provides for the reconstructing and widening of US Route 202 (DeKalb Pike) for approximately 1.8 miles from two lanes to a four-lane cross-section consisting of two travel lanes northbound, a center turn lane, and one travel lane southbound between Johnson Highway and Township Line Road in the Municipality of Norristown, East Norriton & Whitpain Townships. Five-foot bicycle lanes will be provided in both directions along the entire project area, along with new sidewalks and ADA ramps. The project will construct a new precast concrete box culvert, two new sound walls, and a new bridge, as well as install new traffic signals, traffic cameras, and a dynamic message sign. The project also involves major aerial and underground utility relocations and installations for PECO Electric, PECO Gas, Verizon, Comcast, Pennsylvania American Water, and AQUA Pennsylvania sanitary sewer, on Johnson Highway, Dekalb Pike, Germantown Pike, Dekalb Boulevard, and Township Line Road. This section is designed under Section 610. MPMS #50364 (US 202 Section 610) contained the final design funding for this project. See additional MPMS #'s 63491, 63486, and 63490 for other construction sections of Section 600. In the DVRPC region, US 202 covers 61 miles, traversing 27 municipalities in Delaware, Chester, Montgomery, and Bucks counties. For planning purposes, US 202 has been divided into seven major sections (100 through 700), and some of those sections have been broken down further to simplify construction management. Project CMP (Congestion Management Process) commitments include strategies such as improvements for transit users, bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers on the existing road network (operations). See DVRPC's 2007 annual memoranda on supplemental strategies for details related to this project.

title: Washington Lane Bridge
description: The project will rehabilitate the Washington Lane (PA State Route 73) Bridge over SEPTA railroad tracks in Cheltenham Township, which is currently in poor condition. The project will address Priority 0 deficiencies found during bridge inspections including: deteriorated deck joints, excessively corroded and over-extended bearing locations, corroded end diaphragms and stringer ends, and locations where the paint system has failed.

title: Cross County Trail East - Section B
description: This project is proposed to develop a multi-use trail from near Maryland Road near Easton Road to the Willow Grove YMCA in Upper Moreland Township. The Cross County Trail is part of the Circuit Trails network and this segment will serve as an important local and regional transportation resource. The Circuit is a planned 800-mile interconnected network of multi-use trails spanning Greater Philadelphia with Philadelphia and Camden as its hub, and is included in DVRPC's Long-Range Plan. Existing and future Circuit Trails are required to meet minimum design standards (10-feet wide, paved, and separated from traffic with limited exceptions) to reflect their intended use as the arteries of a dedicated, regional, non-motorized transportation system.

title: Dreshertown Road over Br. Sandy Run
description: This project involves rehabilitating or replacing the bridge at Dreshertown Road over a branch of Sandy Run in Upper Dublin Township. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Ridge/Germantown Intersection Realignment - Phase 1, Perkiomen Crossing
description: This intersection realignment project in Lower Providence Township will replace the intersection of Germantown Pike, Ridge Pike, and River Road, which currently sits near the Ridge Pike Bridge over Perkiomen Creek, with two separate intersections to the east in order to reduce congestion and improve traffic flow through this corridor. The first replaced intersection will relocate River Road leading into Germantown Pike, utilizing a roundabout configuration. The second intersection will be signalized and will connect Ridge Pike with a re-aligned Germantown Pike south of the new roundabout. Reconfiguring these intersections will improve safety and mobility in the project area by increasing the spacing between the existing bridge and the new Ridge Pike and Germantown Pike intersection. The roundabout will direct traffic more efficiently to the new signal controlled intersection on Ridge Pike. In addition, a short new connector road will be built between Ridge Pike and Pechins Mill Road to provide access to residents along Pechins Mill Road, which is also being realigned to improve traffic flow. These advance operational improvements are considered Phase 1 of a future improved crossing of the Perkiomen Creek being proposed due to congestion and safety issues where Germantown Pike, Ridge Pike, Main Street, and PA State Route 29 converge on both sides of the creek. The Ridge Pike Bridge over Perkiomen Creek was constructed in 1791 and is the second oldest stone arch structure in Pennsylvania. Additional improvements in Collegeville are currently being advanced as part of an HOP to realign First and Second Avenue and eliminate offset intersections. A future Phase 2 Second Collegeville/Perkiomen Crossing south of the existing stone arch bridge is planned, but due to impacts to wetlands, floodplains, parks, threatened and endangered species, and archaeology, Phase 1 operational improvements will be constructed in advance of a new crossing and will be evaluated for traffic impacts. The Phase 1 improvements are required before a second bridge can be constructed as they will provide connectivity for the second bridge with the existing roadway network.

title: Ridge Pike: Belvoir Road to Chemical Road
description: Ridge Pike is a Montgomery County-owned principal arterial on the National Highway System. This project, known as Section B of the County's Ridge Pike Improvement Project program, is currently in construction, and will provide a center left turn lane to the existing four lane cross-section. Associated construction work includes full-depth pavement reconstruction and drainage replacement; replacement of the existing bridge over Norfolk Southern Railroad (handled with project MPMS #92839); rehabilitation of the bridges over Plymouth Creek and Interstate 476 (Blue Route); upgrading and adding new traffic signals; fiber optic traffic signal interconnections; new sidewalks; and improved transit stops. The overall project extent for Section B is from Belvoir Road to Chemical Road.

title: PA 23 Moore to Allendale and Trout Crk Rd Bridge
description: This project will replace a poor condition, functionally obsolete, weight restricted (15 tons) bridge of Valley Forge Road (PA State Route 23) over Trout Creek in Upper Merion Township. The bridge will be located on a new alignment to eliminate a 90 degree turn on the western end of the bridge and the adjacent stop controlled intersection at Mancill Mill Road. The new bridge and roadway between Moore Road and Vandenberg Road will be two lanes westbound and one lane eastbound, along with new traffic signals at the Mancill Mill and Beidler Road intersections.

title: PA 63, PA 152, Norristown Road at Maple Glen Triangle
description: The Maple Glen Triangle (Triangle), formed by PA State Route 63 (Welsh Road), SR 2052 (Norristown Road), and PA State Route 152 (Limekiln Pike), is located in Upper Dublin and Horsham Townships in Montgomery County. The Triangle includes small to medium-sized businesses offering a variety of personal and convenience services. Outside of the Triangle, residential developments are present along the three roads. The signalized intersections at each corner of the Triangle do not provide adequate capacity to maintain proper traffic flow. On each leg of the Triangle, lack of controlled access prohibits proper circulation through the area and places an added strain on the already stressed intersections. The proposed project involves the following improvements to the Triangle: * New traffic signal equipment and timing/phasing modifications at the signalized intersections of Welsh Road/Norristown Road, Limekiln Pike/Norristown Road, and Welsh Road/Limekiln Pike * Roadway widening along Welsh Road to provide for a three- lane section and dedicated turning lanes where warranted * Roadway widening along Norristown Road to provide for dedicated turning lanes where warranted and enough width to allow for the potential installation of bike lanes as part of a future project * Reconstruction of Limekiln Pike to reconfigure lanes in coordination with Welsh Road and Norristown Road improvements * Elimination of continuous curb cuts and creation of centralized driveways * New sidewalk and ADA upgrades * Roadway drainage improvements To maintain traffic throughout construction, the project will be constructed in three stages. The first two stages will use traffic shifts to allow for one travel lane in each direction while half of the road is under construction. The third stage will use short-term traffic control measures to complete the construction. Construction is anticipated to begin in late 2027 (as of late 2025) and be substantially completed by 2030. The project limits are as follows: SR 63: 1200' south of Norristown Road intersection to 1200' north of Limekiln Pike intersection SR 2052: 800' west of Limekiln Pike intersection to 800' east of Welsh Road intersection SR 0152: 900' south of Norristown Road intersection to 900' north of Welsh Road intersection

title: Montgomery County Bridge Preservation
description: Bridge repair and preservation activities.

title: Penllyn Pike Bridge Replacement (CB #289)
description: This project involves the replacement of the bridge that carries Penllyn Pike (also known as Penllyn-Blue Bell Pike) over Wissahickon Creek, in Whitpain Township. The bridge was constructed in 1964. It is anticipated that the proposed bridge will be replaced on the existing horizontal alignment with minimal approach work to tie back into existing conditions. A final alternative for the bridge replacement will be determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: US 422 Expressway Section M1B
description: This project will reconstruct approximately 1.7 miles of US Route 422 expressway from the Sanatoga interchange to the Norfolk Southern railroad tracks just west of Porter Road in Limerick and Lower Pottsgrove Townships. A culvert at Sprogels Run, located just east of Porter Road, along with an existing single-span bridge carrying US Route 422 over Porter Road, will be removed and replaced with a new two-span bridge. The bridge carrying US Route 422 over Sanatoga Road and Sanatoga Creek will also be reconstructed and widened. The expressway will be reconstructed on both existing and revised alignments to improve horizontal radii, shoulder widths, and vertical clearance to enhance travel and safety. Additional improvements under this project include: reconstructing and lengthening the acceleration ramp from the Sanatoga Interchange (Township Line Road) to westbound US Route 422; installing Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) equipment and components along the US Route 422 corridor and on arterial roadways; constructing sound barriers along portions of westbound US Route 422; upgrading existing and installing new signing; replacing the closed system drainage system and cross culverts throughout the project limits; and improving stormwater management facilities, including two extended detention basins. For additional information on US Route 422 project in the Pottstown area, see MPMS #s 14698, 64220, 64222, 84308, and 66986.

title: Gilbertsville Rd over Ministers Creek
description: This project involves the replacement of the bridge carrying Gilbertsville Road over Ministers Creek in Douglass Township. Â The project is in the final design phase.

title: Penn's Landing Project Development - Local DEVELOPMENT - LOCAL
description: This project will involve the landscaping, building and amenities portion of the I-95 CAP project being paid for by local and private dollars. 12/3/2021-- This project has been created for the items that are essential for functioning of the public spaces but not eligible for transportation funding. The funding for this portion of the work is City of Philadelphia bond and private. This second contract will be let under an open bid by the Delaware River Waterfront Corporation, a registered 501(c)3 nonprofit corporation that acts as the steward of the waterfront and funded in part by the City. The parameters for the ownership, responsibility, and maintenance of all the cap components listed above are identified in a license agreement with the City that is currently in the process of execution. The Department will only be responsible for the heavy infrastructure with all landscape, building and amenities being the responsibility of the City and DRWC. Agreement language has been developed by the Office of Chief Counsel, Counsel for Department of General Services, and the office of the City Solicitor.

title: 63rd Street Corridor Safety Improvements
description: This is the Parent project that involves safety improvements along the entire 6.9 mile corridor of 63rd Street/Cobbs Creek (SR 3015) from City to Woodland Avenues. Individual projects will go to construction as funding becomes available. The proposed scope of this project includes, but is not limited to: * Traffic signal improvements (modernization of signal equipment which includes mast arms, upgrade 8 to 12 signal heads, second overhead signals where required, LPIs, countdown pedestrian signal heads, controllers, signal timing/phasing improvements updates, pavement marking and signing upgrades. * Road Diet, a reduction from 4 travel lanes to 2 travel lanes and a center two-way left turn lane. * Median & pedestrian crossing islands * Raised center medians * Improve pedestrian crossing facilities by providing raised crossing walks and rectangular rapid flashing beacons (RRFB) at identified locations * Guiderail and street lighting upgrades

title: 30th Street Viaduct over 30th Street Lower (Bridge)
description: The purpose of the project is to rehabilitate the 30th Street Viaduct over 30th Street Lower between Market Street and Walnut Street to extend the useful life of the bridge. Work is planned to include deck replacement, superstructure and substructure cleaning & repair, and possible further rehabilitation. The underside of the bridge superstructure will be cleaned and repainted, with steel repairs as necessary. The bridge's drainage system will also be replaced and upgraded as needed. Recent bridge repairs have revealed accelerated deterioration of the structure, which will continue to worsen without rehabilitation, and could result in eventual weight restrictions or closure. Recent high-density development in the area has increased use of the viaduct, and pending future developments in the 30th Street Station area will further increase its importance, making future restrictions or closures highly disruptive.

title: Falls Road Bridge
description: This project is for improvements to the Falls Road Bridge in Philadelphia to extend its useful life. The bridge is currently considered in poor condition, with a five-ton posted weight limit and a sufficiency rating of 13, and will continue to deteriorate without rehabilitation. Anticipated work includes demolition and replacement of the existing deck and floorbeams, bearing replacement, repairs to existing stone abutments, repairs to select steel truss members and pins, repainting of existing superstructure steel, full depth roadway reconstruction & limited repaving, curb & sidewalk reconstruction (including ADA curb ramp construction), street lighting improvements, and other miscellaneous construction. The current cross-section will be maintained, as will the significant character-defining features of this National Register-eligible structure. This project is a component of the County Bridge Line Item (MPMS #95447).

title: Spring Garden Connector
description: To develop a complete street design for Spring Garden Street, in order to better and more safely accommodate all road users, contribute to the sense of place on the corridor, advance the city's green stormwater management and traffic safety goals, and complete the Center City section of the East Coast Greenway Spring Garden Street's current configuration and state of repair does not provide adequate access or safety, resulting in decreased levels of service as well as conflicts and unsafe conditions for all road users. Design is funded locally with $500,000 of Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) funds, $1,000,000 City Capital, $1,000,000 PA DCNR Funds, and $2,000,000 of private funds.

title: Benjamin Franklin Bridge Preservation
description: This project will replace the pavement on the Ben Franklin Bridge and approach roadways. The project will also reconstruct and rehabilitate the bridge expansion joints on the suspension spans and approach spans. The project will also replace existing overhead guide signs on the bridge for eastbound traffic, and repair deteriorated concrete on the ceiling and walls of the 5th Street Pedestrian Tunnel.

title: 63rd / Cobbs Creek Phase 3
description: Safety improvements on 63rd Street/ Cobbs Creek Pkwy for the 3rd phase of the 6.9 mile corridor. Ongoing coordination with The City of Philadelphia and SEPTA, the project will be fine-tuned in the future. Currently, improvements are anticipated to include: - Install a modified road diet from Girard Ave to Market Street. - Install curb bump outs/extensions at select intersections from Lebanon Avenue to Race Street. - Install bus boarding islands from Jefferson Street to Race Street. - Full signal upgrades from Girard Ave to Race Street. - Partial signal upgrades from City Avenue to Haverford Avenue and Church Street to Woodland Avenue. Design activities will be completed under the parent project, 63rd Street Corridor Safety Improvements (MPMS #115435).

title: Willits Road Bridge Over Wooden Bridge Run
description: This project involves rehabilitating or replacing the bridge carrying Willits Road (S.R. 1011) over Wooden Bridge Run in the City of Philadelphia. The purpose of the project is to extend the service life of the existing structure. The existing structure has severely rusted components, large open spalls exposing rusted reinforced steel, and cracks with efflorescence. Work will include replacing or rehabilitating the existing superstructure and reinforced concrete overlay. The project could also include upgrades to the guiderail approaches. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement is determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Tabor Road over Tacony Creek (Bridge)
description: Tabor Road bridge is located at the crossing of Tacony Creek in Philadelphia, Philadelphia County Pennsylvania. The structure is located 250 ft east of the intersection of Bingham Street and Tabor Road. The bridge carrying Tabor Road over Tacony Creek is a three span, non-composite, adjacent box beam bridge that was built in 1957. The existing structure is in overall poor condition. Soil slopes in front of the abutments are in poor condition, especially the eastern (far) abutment, exhibiting erosion. The proposed scope of work includes the following: demolition and removal of the existing superstructure, including the barriers, sidewalks, deck, and prestressed concrete adjacent box beams; construction of a proposed superstructure with vertical concrete barriers, sidewalks, and a reinforced concrete deck atop composite continuous steel beams; substructure rehabilitation; full depth roadway reconstruction plus limited areas of resurfacing; intersection reconstruction at Tabor Road and Olney Avenue/Bingham Street, including new curb bump-outs, new ADA ramps, pavement mill and overlay, and new traffic signals; upgrade stormwater infrastructure within project limits; relocate utilities (Electric, Gas, and Water) to facilitate construction and to minimize service outages. Due to the nature of proposed rehabilitation work, vehicular traffic will be detoured for the entirety of construction. Bicyclists and pedestrians will be detoured for 4 months. This project is a component of the County Bridge Line Item (MPMS #95447).

title: Citywide ADA Ramps 4
description: This "Transition List" project will include the design and construction of ADA ramps that were originally included in the scope of other federal aid projects as well as various streetscape projects and ramps located on select Federal Aid routes that were repaved with local funding. These ramps typically would be included as design build items in the original project contracts, however, in some instances, the urban context of the ADA ramp locations warrants further coordination or study. To allow the original construction projects to proceed in a timely fashion, these ramps were pulled from the original construction contracts and will now be addressed as part of this transition list package. This will allow the City to design and construct the ramps to meet current ADA requirements while properly providing for stairs, cellar doors, unique paving materials, adjacent historic properties and other considerations as necessary.

title: 70th, 71st, 72nd Streets over Amtrak
description: Rehabilitation of 70th, 71st and 72nd Street Bridges over rail facilities and upgrades of adjacent intersections. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement is determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance. The 71st and 72nd St. bridges were previously determined eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places.

title: US 1: Broad Street - Adams Avenue
description: Intersection and roadway improvements along US 1 from Broad Street to Pratt Street in the City of Philadelphia. The design of the project will be funded by ASE funding and CON will be partially funded by the MEGA grant. Improvements include curb extensions to shorten crossing distances, realigned crosswalks, realigned lane configurations and turn lanes, upgrades to traffic signals and timing, changes to traffic movements, and new or upgraded transit shelters and stations.

title: Spring Garden over Amtrak
description: The existing structure is an 11-Span Prestressed Concrete Adjacent Box Beam Bridge plus Single-Span Steel Girder Floorbeam Bridge. The bridge serves as an essential connection point between Mantua/Powelton Village and Fairmount/Center City. Spanning over several railroad lines, and traversing underneath the CSX High Line Bridge, the structure is in poor condition due to deterioration of both the superstructure and substructure. Structure rehabilitation is needed to extend the bridge's service life for continued use by motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists. This project will rehabilitate or replace the Spring Garden Street Bridges over rail facilities, north of 30th St. Station. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement is determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: PA Transportation and Community Development Initiative (TCDI)
description: The Transportation and Community Development Initiative (TCDI) is a grant program that supports smart growth in the individual municipalities of the Delaware Valley through initiatives that implement the regions long-range plan, Connections 2050 Plan for Greater Philadelphia. Central to the effort is the objective to enhance quality of life choices by providing and maintaining essential infrastructure, supporting local and regional economic development, and linking land use and transportation planning. TCDI provides a mechanism for our planning partners to undertake locally-directed actions to improve their communities, which in turn implements their local county comprehensive plans and supports the goals and vision of the regions long-range plan. This grant program seeks to support and leverage state and county programs, by providing funding to undertake planning, analysis or early-stage design projects which improve the efficiency of the regional transportation system. Through a competitive selection process, DVRPC will award $1.6 million to select projects in the 5-county Pennsylvania region which includes the counties of Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery and Philadelphia. Tasks 1. Distribute $1.6 million dollars to selected projects within Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia Counties. See MPMS #64652

title: I-95 Central Access Philadelphia (CAP) / Waterfront Access
description: This project creates an innovative complex of a cap structure, viaduct, road, and trail structures that re-establish a strong connection between central Philadelphia and its waterfront, while making multi-modal enhancements that improve the transportation experience for pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles. The new cap/bridge structure will span both I-95 and Christopher Columbus Boulevard between Chestnut and Walnut Streets, providing more direct access to the waterfront. The scope of this project includes 5 major components: 1) replacing and expanding the existing cap/bridge structure near Penn's Landing and constructing a new, extended cap/bridge structure which will span both I-95 and Christopher Columbus Boulevard between Chestnut and Walnut Streets for pedestrian and vehicular use (note the current cap extends from Chestnut Street to Sansom Walk, and only Chestnut Street and Walnut Street span Columbus Boulevard); 2) extending the South Street pedestrian bridge from the east edge of I-95 northbound over Columbus Boulevard to Penn's Landing; 3) reconstructing the viaduct connection between Chestnut and Market Streets at Penn's Landing; 4) constructing a section of the Delaware River Trail along Christopher Columbus Boulevard; and 5) inspection and repairs of underwater concrete piles located in the Penn's Landing area.

title: Cobbs Creek Parkway: Market - Woodland
description: This project will construct safety improvements on Cobbs Creek Parkway for the 1st phase of the 6.9 mile corridor. The project area involves coordination with various City of Philadelphia departments including Philadelphia Water Department, Rebuild, and SEPTA. Improvements include: * Full signal upgrade from Chestnut Street to Springfield Avenue (13 signals) * Install/Upgrade pedestrian crossings at select intersections from Locust St. to 67th Street. * Install curb bump out/extensions at Market Street, Walnut Street, and Spruce Street. * Install a modified road diet from Market Street to Spruce Street. * Install a center median island from Spruce Street to 59th Street and Hoffman Avenue to 60th Street. * Street lighting improvements from Market Street to Springfield Avenue. * Guide rail replacement from Larchwood Street to 62nd Street and Hoffman Avenue to Springfield Avenue. Design activities will be completed under the parent project, 63rd Street Corridor Safety Improvements (MPMS #115435).

title: Market Street Bridges (3) Over Schuylkill River and CSX Railroad (MSB)
description: This project involves the rehabilitation of the 2-span bridge carrying Market Street over the Schuylkill River , the replacement of the bridge carrying Market Street over the Schuylkill River Park and CSX railroad from a 4-span bridge to a 1-span bridge, and replacement of the 3-span Market Street bridge over I-76 at the Schuylkill Avenue West intersection in the City of Philadelphia. The 2 span, 361'-long concrete encased steel arch bridge over the Schuylkill River was built in 1932 and is finished with limestone spandrel walls and fascia rings. Concrete urn-shaped balustrades and statues decorate the structure, although a quadrant of the balustrade has been filled with concrete. The bridge is significant as a contributing resource to the 30th Street Station Historic District. This bridge was previously determined eligible for listing in the National Register. The project includes the repairing and patching of the parapets and sidewalks as needed, replacement/repair of the deck and beams, and replacement of cobrahead lighting. The bridge is poor condition due to severe rust in in the substructure and spalling in the superstructure. The 4 span, 216' long built up deck girder bridge over CSX railroad, built in 1932, is supported on concrete abutments and three steel pier bents, of which two are encased in concrete. This bridge was previously determined ineligible for listing in the National Register. This bridge will be replaced with a 1 span bridge with wider sidewalks. The 3 span bridge over I-76 at the Schuylkill Avenue West intersection was built in 1932 and significantly modified in the late 1950s when I-76 was constructed. The bridge has significantly deteriorated and will be replaced. Pedestrian and bicycle improvements are being coordinated with the City of Philadelphia throughout the project.

title: Schuylkill Banks: Batram-Passyunk Phase 2
description: This project is to acquire land and construct a 3,400-foot extension of the Schuylkill Banks trail, thereby connecting Philadelphia's greater trail network to the pedestrian infrastructure and public transportation routes along Passyunk Avenue, which is a major thoroughfare connecting multiple communities throughout South and Southwest Philadelphia. Schuylkill River Development Corporation (SRDC) will help manage land acquisition and construction in partnership with the City of Philadelphia, the eventual project site owner. Acquiring land and constructing the Bartram's to Passyunk Phase 2 trail segment ensures the expansion of low- and no-cost transportation options to more residents, encourages new bicycle and pedestrian trips between dozens of Philadelphia neighborhoods and transportation hubs, and increases multimodal transportation throughout the city. Additionally, completing the project ensures the fair and equitable distribution of high-quality transportation facilities to underserved populations in Southwest Philadelphia.

title: Philadelphia Bridge Preservation
description: Bridge repair and preservation activities.

title: Bells Mill Road and Valley Green Road over Wissahickon Creek
description: Built in the 1800s, the Bells Mill Road and Valley Green Road bridges provide access to Wissahickon Valley Park, one of the citys noteworthy natural destinations, which experiences frequent flooding. Work includes bridge restoration, roadway rehabilitation, drainage improvements, guide rail replacement, and watershed improvements to reduce impacts from flooding and extreme weather events. Improvements also include restoration and creation of wetlands. See also MPMS #17581. The Bells Mill Road Bridge is the only transportation link between the Roxborough and Chestnut Hill neighborhoods of Philadelphia. It is a key connector between the Ridge Avenue and Germantown Avenue corridors, both of which are heavily traveled. Additionally, the bridge provides motorists with access to Chestnut Hill Hospital. The Bells Mill Road Bridge also facilitates access to Wissahickon Valley Park and directly intersects with Forbidden Drive, a multi-use trail that traverses Wissahickon Valley Park's entire length. Forbidden Drive is a core part of the Philadelphia Circuit Trails network, connecting with other multi-use trails regionwide. The Valley Green Road Bridge, which crosses the Wissahickon Creek, is more recreational and is actively used by pedestrians and cyclists. For motorists, the Valley Green Road Bridge has less regional connectivity than the bridge on Bells Mill Road. However, the Valley Green Road Bridge remains an integral gateway to the Wissahickon Valley Park, especially for pedestrians and cyclists. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement is determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Ridge Ave Over Amtrak (Bridge)
description: This project invoves rehabiltating or replacing the Ridge Avenue Bridge over AMTRAK in Philadelphia. A final alternative for bridge rehabilitation or replacement is determined upon federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) or state Categorical Exclusion clearance.

title: Philadelphia Interconnected Solutions to Accelerate Alternative Fuel Transportation
description: The Corridor project will install four dual port DCFC fast-chargers with the Cell Phone Waiting Lot at Philadelphia International Airport (PHL). The project will fill the gap in the charging network and proximity to the next available charging location.

title: 59th Street over AMTRAK (Bridge)
description: This project is a bridge replacement of 59th Street over AMTRAK in the City of Philadelpia. The current structure was built in 1926, and consists of a four simple-span, partially concrete-encased-steel girder/floorbeam/jackarch superstructure atop reinforced concrete abutment and pier substructures. The anticipated work includes demolition and removal of the existing superstructure and portions of the existing reinforced concrete abutments & piers and construction of a new steel multi-girder bridge with reinforced concrete composite deck atop reinforced concrete abutments and piers; as well as roadway approach reconstruction and repaving, curb and sidewalk reconstruction, a new high-quality bicycle facility, streetlighting improvements, ADA accessibility improvements, railroad electric traction (ET) system modification and utility relocations, and other related work. This project is a component of the County Bridge Line Item (MPMS #95447).

title: Philadelphia Vision Zero Capital Plan Implementation Project
description: The Philadelphia Vision Zero Capital Plan Implementation project will implement traffic safety improvements along priority Vision Zero corridors that are disproportionately impacted by traffic crashes. Construction improvements will focus on systematically applying multiple proven safety countermeasures at intersections and other vulnerable areas. These improvements will include raised medians and pedestrian refuge islands, raised pedestrian crossings, roadway and intersection modifications, traffic signal improvements, speed management measures, corridor access management strategies, and other transportation infrastructure upgrades.

title: Complete & Safe Streets Philadelphia: Vision Zero High Injury Network Corridors
description: The Complete & Safe Streets Philadelphia: Vision Zero High Injury Network Corridors Project will build critically needed protected bike infrastructure along corridors that are part of the High-Injury Network (HIN), and transportation safety improvements along key corridors located in historically disadvantaged communities and areas of persistent poverty. The City will use funds to advance final design and construction for bicycle lane separation and traffic calming demonstration projects and construction for the High Injury Network priority projects. The City expects to use funds to complete final design for bicycle lanes on approximately ten centerline miles of roadway, all on roadway segments identified as part of both the High- Quality Bike Network and the High Injury Network. Hunting Park - This is an important corridor that connects through multiple neighborhoods. It is on the High Injury Network, part of the High-Quality Bike Network, and identified as a priority corridor in the Vision Zero Capital Plan. The corridor is an important transit route, serving multiple bus routes including a forthcoming Direct Bus, continuing the Direct Bus connections from Roosevelt Boulevard. There is a transit hub at Wissahickon Avenue and a major high school, among other destinations. Currently, DVRPC is evaluating a separated side path to improve the corridor's level of biking and walking safety. Old York Road - This north/south corridor crosses Hunting Park Avenue and Roosevelt Boulevard, connecting multiple neighborhoods and existing/planned bike routes. It is on the High Injury Network. Design funding was approved through the 2022 Safe Streets for All award, and additional funding would see the project through construction and implementation.

title: Aramingo/Harbison: Church Street to Amtrak (Section BS3)
description: This project is a component of the Statewide Interstate Management Program (IMP) and is a construction breakout from Section BSR (MPMS #47811 ). This phase of SR 95 Section BSR covers the reconstruction of Aramingo Avenue from Church Street to Tacony Street, and the reconstruction of Harbison Avenue from Tacony Street to Torresdale Avenue, including traffic signal modifications at the following intersections: -Aramingo Avenue at Orthodox Street -Aramingo Avenue at Margaret Street -Aramingo/Harbison Avenues at Tacony Street -Harbison Avenue at Tacony Street/Wakeling Street -Harbison Avenue at Tacony Street/Wakeling Street -Harbison Avenue at Bridge Street -Harbison Avenue at Torresdale Avenue This project will construct a multi-use sidepath on the east side of Aramingo Avenue from Church Street to Orthodox Street and Margaret Street. The existing bicycle lanes and the sidewalk on the east side of Aramingo Avenue will be removed. Also, the area vacated by the removal of the southbound I-95 on-ramp in the BR4 project (MPMS #103559) will be converted to a community amenity. The existing veterans' memorial will be preserved. For an overall description of the SR 95 Section BSR section see MPMS #47811. description: This project will design and construct multimodal improvements to Benjamin Franklin Parkway, including the Eakins Oval in front of the Philadelphia Museum of Art Steps and the adjacent Pennsylvania Avenue.
